title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 146 (Auditors to attend general meeting)

content.overview: All notices of, and other communications relating to, any general meeting shall be forwarded to the auditor of the company, and the auditor shall, unless otherwise exempted by the company, attend either by himself or through his authorised representative, who shall also be qualified to be an auditor, any general meeting and shall have right to be heard at such meeting on any part of the business which concerns him as the auditor.
content.glance: Auditor receives notice of every general meeting, attends unless exempted, and has a right to be heard on business concerning him as auditor.
content.study:
## Section 146 — Auditors to attend general meeting

**Notice.** All notices and other communications relating to any general meeting must be forwarded to the auditor.

**Attendance.** The auditor shall attend, either personally or through an authorised representative who is also qualified to be an auditor, unless the company exempts him.

**Right to be heard.** On any part of the business which concerns him as auditor. The right is to be heard, not to vote.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Notice and attendance
sections.body: Notice to auditor; attend unless exempted (personally or by qualified authorised representative).

sections.heading: Right to be heard
sections.body: On business concerning him as auditor; not a right to vote.

examples.title: Auditor at AGM
examples.body: Company forwards AGM notice to the auditor, who attends and is heard on the audit report. Educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Must the auditor vote at the general meeting?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 146 gives a right to be heard on business concerning him as auditor, not a right to vote.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the auditor as a voting member at the general meeting.
misconceptions.correction: Section 146 confers attendance and a right to be heard, not a vote.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Notice of general meetings to the auditor; attendance unless exempted; right to be heard on business concerning him as auditor.
